thread:
IncidentBot: 🚨 INCIDENT detected: routing.fallback.loop → spike in cross-region fallbacks and model-variant mismatches. paging on-call @marta. root: smart-routing.policy.v2.

Marta (on-call): on it. seeing a steady rise in error-rate and tail latency 5m. looks like fallbacks are ping-ponging between eu-west and us-central. grabbing logs.

Sam (sre): FYI I pushed a temporary model-pin yesterday to v2-small to reduce memory pressure for a few customers. did anyone also force-region?

Jia (infra): I see a manual override entry around 1961121200 in the routing-audit: `force_region(customer=acme, region=us-central)` and a later `force_variant(customer=acme, variant=v2-small)` at 1961121900. Those overrides bypass the usual fallback compatibility check.

Alex (prodops): That force_variant was because acme reported higher p99 latency on the new large variant. Ops followed the playbook to avoid customer impact. didn't realize the fallback policy would start bouncing other customers.

Marta (on-call): aha — looks like the override created sticky routing rules for the serving tiers. when regional capacity drops, smart-router attempts fallback but the pinned variant/region is incompatible, so it forces a fallback to a different region, which then triggers the pinned rule again. loop.

OpsBot: autodetect: fallback-loop-count=18 in last 10m, affected-routes=12, estimated-customer-impact=8%.

CustomerSuccess (cs): multiple customers reporting errors and timeouts. acme reported 503s on streams, also a twitchy enterprise customer on Dedicated. escalating.

Sam (sre): propose steps: 1) remove the `force_region` override for acme, 2) remove model pin for acme, 3) restore fallback_policy to safe-default (prefer-local + variant-compatibility), 4) flush prefix cache on routers.

Jia (infra): agree but note: removing overrides abruptly will route >50% traffic to their default variant which may still be overloaded. recommend a staggered unwind: unpin variant first, monitor, then unpin region.

Marta (on-call): OK do staggered. Sam you can execute the unpin. Jia do the cache flush/monitoring hooks. Alex coordinate comms with CS. will page if any spike.

Sam (sre): running command now:
```
# unpin variant for acme
redwoodctl overrides remove --customer acme --type variant --id force_variant_1961121900
```

Sam (sre): done. override removed at 1961122203. watching error rates.

OpsBot: metric update: error-rate -> 3.4% (was 5.1%), fallback-loop-count -> 9.

Marta (on-call): good. Jia proceed with prefix cache flush on the regional routers for us-central/eu-west.

Jia (infra): running flush:
```
curl -XPOST https://router-api.internal/flush_prefix_cache -d '{"regions":["us-central","eu-west"]}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED'
```

Jia (infra): cache flush acknowledged, restart of routing-proxy pods queued for 30s rolling restart to avoid traffic cliff.

Alex (prodops): notifying CS and posting interim status to acme: "we are unwinding a temporary override that caused routing instability; small chance of transient increased latency; monitoring closely". :phone:

CustomerSuccess (cs): acme acknowledged, asked for ETA. mention they'll pause some heavy batch jobs.

Marta (on-call): OpsBot, what's tail-latency now?

OpsBot: p95 latency down from 1.8s to 1.2s, p99 still 2.6s. loops reduced to 3 in last 5m.

Sam (sre): rolling restart finished. I'm seeing a small spike at restart time but traffic rebalanced. continuing to monitor.

Marta (on-call): next: remove the `force_region` entry once we're confident. Jia, any blockers?

Jia (infra): no blockers. I'll wait for one more 5m stable window then remove.

Marta (on-call): copy. if anything regresses, we fallback to canary throttle (route 10% to low-latency pool) and re-pin for acme but with compatibility mode on.

Jia (infra): removing force_region now:
```
redwoodctl overrides remove --customer acme --type region --id force_region_1961121200
```

Jia (infra): removed at 1961122435. Monitoring.

OpsBot: final check: fallback-loop-count=0 in last 2m, error-rate=0.9%, p99=1.1s. Impacted routes normalized.

Marta (on-call): great. we'll keep an eye for 1h. Sam please follow up with a postmortem entry documenting why we used force- overrides instead of canary throttles and add a guard: `overrides` cannot be applied without variant-compatibility flag. Jia add an automated alert when force_* overrides are created.

Sam (sre): will add runbook step to prefer canary-throttle in the future.

Jia (infra): I'll add the alert + a quick lint in the web UI to block override submissions that omit compatibility checks.

Alex (prodops): CS will craft an incident blurb for customers. we should note duration, affected percent, and mitigation steps.

CustomerSuccess (cs): acme's ops says impact window ~12m, they accepted the explanation and thanked us for quick rollback.

Marta (on-call): handing off to Sam for the next 60m watch. I'll update on-call rotation if anything else pops. closing this thread but keeping notes in the incident tracker. :white_check_mark:

IncidentBot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: routing.fallback.loop -> mitigation applied; severity: S3 -> monitoring. RCA assigned to Sam/Jia.
